sentences.text: This is a suit filed by the plaintiff against the defendant seeking the relief of judgment and decree of permanent injunction.

2. The brief averments of the plaint is as follows: -
The plaintiff is the absolute owner and in possession and enjoyment of suit schedule property.
The plaintiff purchased the suit schedule property for valuable consideration from one Munivenkatappa.
The said the property was the ancestral property of the said Munivenkatappa.
The said Munivenkatappa was the owner and in possession of the suit schedule property.
The ownership of the said Munivenkatappa was duly recognised by the authorities earlier in the revenue records.

The said Munivenkatappa for and on behalf of his family sold suit schedule property which was vacant site for valuable consideration in favour of husband of the plaintiff by name H.N. Krishnareddy in the year 1996.
The said Munivenkatappa also executed an Irrevocable General Power of Attorney in favour of Krishnareddy on 07.06.1996.
Since then husband of the plaintiff was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said property.

The plaintiff further contends that, she purchased the suit schedule property for valuable consideration from Munivenkatappa through his agent and they have executed Registered Sale Deed dated 21.04.2005.
The plaintiff was duly put in possession of the suit schedule property.
Later on, the plaintiff by spending huge amount put up asbestos sheet roofed 2 commercial shops in the suit schedule property.
The ward number was wrongly described in the schedule of the principal Sale Deed as Ward No.74.
The said mistake was duly corrected under a Registered Rectification Deed dated 04.05.2005.
The plaintiff has obtained electricity service connection from the BESCOM authority.
The plaintiff also used to pay tax to the BBMP.
Thus, the plaintiff is in absolute physical possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property without any interruption from the third parties.
The plaintiff contends that, earlier one P. Krishnappa and T. Prasannakumar were inducted to the portion of property as tenants.
Since they declined to vacate the shop, the plaintiff filed a civil suit in S.C.No 15797/2011 for their ejectment .
The said the suit came to be decreed by the judgment dated 11.01.2012.
The said tenants were duly evicted through the due process of law by the plaintiff.
The suit filed by the above tenants in O.S.No.26728/2011 for injunction from dispossession came to be dismissed.
All these factors established the exclusive ownership and possession of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
The plaintiff at present inducted 2 tenants in 2 portions of the suit property.

"Having regard to the fact that the acquisition proceedings had been completed way back in 1960- 70, the plaintiffs who purchased the suit land in 1995 cannot have any right to maintain the suit of this nature particularly, against defendant Nos.1 and 2,

Hence, the plaintiff cannot have any right to maintain the suit of this nature particularly, against the defendant/BDA.
19.
Furthermore, the plaintiff has purchased the suit schedule property after coming into force of the Karnataka Land (Restriction on Transfer) Act, 1991.
As per Section 3 and 4 of the said Act, there is a prohibition on transfer of land acquired by the Government.

Any transfer by sale etc., of land situated in urban area which has been acquired by the Government under the Land Acquisition Act 1894 or any other law providing for acquisition of land for a public purpose, no person shall, except with previous permission in writing on the competent authority, transfer or purport to transfer by sale, mortgage, gift, lease or otherwise any land or part thereof situated in any urban area which is proposed to be acquired in connection with the scheme in relation to which the declaration has been published under Section 19 of Bangalore Development Authority Act, 1976.
In the case on hand, the plaintiff has not obtained any permission in writing from the defendant before purchasing the land as per Ex.P.1 and P.6.
Hence, there was a prohibition for the plaintiff to purchase the suit schedule property when the defendant had already acquired the said property.
20. The plaintiff is seeking an injunction against the true owner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in (2021) 3 SCC 675; A.Subramanian v. R.Panner Selvam has held that, a person in possession of land in the assumed character of owner and exercising peaceably the ordinary rights of ownership has a perfectly good title against all the world but the rightful owner.
Therefore, the plaintiff is not entitled to any injunction or protect his possession against the rightful owner.
More particularly, when he fails to get the declaratory relief and the dispute with respect to the title comes to an end.
21. A person has a right to protect his possession against any person who does not prove a better title by seeking a prohibitory injunction.
But a person in wrongful possession is not entitled to an injunction against the rightful owner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision reported in (2012)
5 SCC 370; Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria held that, due process of law means that nobody ought to be condemned unheard.

entities.text: Maria Margarida Sequeria Fernandes v. Erasmo Jack de Sequeria
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The due process of law means a person in settled possession will not be dispossessed except by due process of law.
Due process means an opportunity to the defendant to file pleadings including written statement and documents before the court of law.
It does not mean the whole trial.
Due process of law is satisfied the moment rights of the parties are adjudicated upon by a competent court.
In the case on hand, after the acquisition of land, the suit property was purchased by the plaintiff.
By that time, the defendant was already a owner of the suit property and suit property was vested with the defendant.
The plaintiff is seeking an order of injunction against the true owner.
Hence, on this count also the plaintiff is not entitled to any order of equitable relief of injunction against the defendant.
As already stated the plaintiff herself has admitted in her cross- examination that suit property is a part of Sy.No. 51 of Dookanahalli/Dhoopanahalli Village.
This survey number was acquired by the defendant very long back on 16.09.1960 itself.
As per Ex.D.1 to D.7 documents, the suit property vested with the defendant.

Hence, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable as per the ruling of Hon'ble Supreme Court, reported in (2013) 3 SCC 66; Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority and another v. Brijesh Reddy and another.

Since then husband of the plaintiff was in peaceful possession and enjoyment of the said property.
The plaintiff further contends that, she purchased the suit schedule property for valuable consideration from Munivenkatappa through his agent and they have executed Registered Sale Deed dated 21.04.2005.
The plaintiff was duly put in possession of the suit schedule property.
The said mistake was duly corrected under a Registered Rectification Deed dated 04.05.2005.
The plaintiff has obtained electricity service connection from the BESCOM authority.
The plaintiff also used to pay tax to the BBMP.
Thus, the plaintiff is in absolute physical possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property without any interruption from the third parties.
Since they declined to vacate the shop, the plaintiff filed a civil suit in S.C.No 15797/2011 for their ejectment .
The suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable.
The plaintiff has not issued the mandatory notice as contemplated under Section 64 of the Bangalore Development Authority Act.
The defendant denied the ownership and possession of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property.
opennyai_summary.issue:
4. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, my predecessor-in-office has framed the following issues for determination:-
ISSUES 1.
Whether plaintiff proves that she is in actual possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property as described in the plaint schedule as on the date of suit?
2. Whether plaintiff proves the alleged interference by the defendant?
3. Whether the plaintiff is entitle for the relief claimed?
4. What order or decree ?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is the case of the plaintiff that, she is in physical possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property and she cannot be dispossessed by the defendant without due process of law.
In the present case, the plaintiff claiming injunction against the BDA in respect of the property acquired in the year 1960.
Furthermore, the plaintiff has purchased the suit schedule property after coming into force of the Karnataka Land (Restriction on Transfer) Act, 1991.
As per Section 3 and 4 of the said Act, there is a prohibition on transfer of land acquired by the Government.
In the case on hand, the plaintiff has not obtained any permission in writing from the defendant before purchasing the land as per Ex.P.1 and P.6.
Hence, there was a prohibition for the plaintiff to purchase the suit schedule property when the defendant had already acquired the said property.
The due process of law means a person in settled possession will not be dispossessed except by due process of law.
Due process means an opportunity to the defendant to file pleadings including written statement and documents before the court of law.
It does not mean the whole trial.
Due process of law is satisfied the moment rights of the parties are adjudicated upon by a competent court.
In the case on hand, after the acquisition of land, the suit property was purchased by the plaintiff.
By that time, the defendant was already a owner of the suit property and suit property was vested with the defendant.
The plaintiff is seeking an order of injunction against the true owner.
Hence, on this count also the plaintiff is not entitled to any order of equitable relief of injunction against the defendant.
Hence, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable as per the ruling of Hon'ble Supreme Court, reported in (2013) 3 SCC 66; Commissioner, Bangalore Development Authority and another v. Brijesh Reddy and another.
The plaintiff is not entitled to equitable relief of permanent injunction.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
16. The learned counsel for defendant argued that, the suit of the plaintiff is not maintainable against the defendant.
The learned counsel for plaintiff has argued that, the defendant has not disputed the settled possession of the plaintiff over the suit schedule property and as such, the settled possession of the plaintiff cannot be dispossessed without recourse of law.
The learned counsel for plaintiff has relied on the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2004) SCC 769; Ramegowda (Dead) by LRs. v. M.Varadappa Naidu (Dead) by LRs and another.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Hence, above Points No.1 to 3 are answered in the negative.
In view of the above discussions, this court proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is hereby dismissed.
Parties to bear their own costs.
